model_result.answer_summary: Tick option (b): increasing [Red] decreases the emission lifetimes of both S1 and T1. Dynamic quenching adds k_q[Red] to the excited-state decay rate, so tau([Red]) = tau0/(1 + k_q tau0 [Red]), which is strictly decreasing because both printed quenching constants and unquenched lifetimes are positive.
assumptions: Standard dynamic bimolecular-quenching kinetics: at fixed reductant concentration c, the quenching channel contributes the pseudo-first-order loss rate k_q c, so independent loss rates add.
Reductant concentrations are nonnegative and all non-quenching decay conditions remain fixed while [Red] is varied.
The printed k_S, k_T, tau0(S1), and tau0(T1) are treated as exact stipulated values for this qualitative classification.
